Smt Madhabilata Mondal vs Sri Haradhan Mondal And Another
on 15 July, 2024
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side
Present:
The Hon'ble Justice Ajay Kumar Gupta

C.R.R. 1437 of 2017
 Smt Madhabilata Mondal
 Versus
 Sri Haradhan Mondal And Another

For the Petitioner : Mr. Sujay Sarkar, Adv.
 Mr. Rahul Chachan, Adv.
Heard on : 22.04.2024 Judgment on : 15.07.2024 Ajay Kumar Gupta, J:
1.

The petitioner being the wife of opposite party no. 1 has filed this revisional application under Sections 397/401 read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 challenging the propriety, legality and correctness of the impugned order dated February 8, 2017 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 2nd Court at Bolpur, Birbhum in connection with Miscellaneous Case No. 178 of 2016, thereby rejecting the petitioner's claim for interim maintenance under Section 23(1) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act.
2.

sentences.text: The petitioner got married with the opposite party no. 1 on 05.06.1990.
Thereafter, the petitioner led conjugal life and she gave birth to a female child.
After three years of marriage, the opposite party no. 1 started physical and mental torture upon the petitioner on demand of more money.
Later the petitioner has come to know that the opposite party no. 1 has an illicit relation with one Sathi Banerjee.
On 05.01.2016 the opposite party no. 1 drove her out in a single cloth in absence of her daughter due to his illicit relationship.
To that effect, petitioner lodged a written complaint against the opposite party no. 1 under Sections 498A/494/307 of the IPC.
Since then, she is residing separately and the opposite party no. 1 never took any information of the petitioner's condition.
Furthermore, he had neglected and refused to maintain her.

Petitioner is unable to maintain herself as she has no income of her own whereas the opposite party no. 1 is an employee of Visva Bharati University and his income is about Rs. 50,000/-
per month.

Accordingly, she made an application under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 2nd Court, Bolpur, Birbhum praying for maintenance at the rate of Rs. 25,000/- per month for herself and Rs. 3,00,000/- for compensation for torture and other reliefs.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2b. The said case was contested by opposite party no. 1 after filing written objection, inter alia,
admiting the fact of marriage between the parties and their daughter but denied all other averments and allegations made by the petitioner.

In the said application, the petitioner has filed an application under Section 23(1) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act for grant of interim maintenance from the opposite party no. 1 but after hearing the parties and considering the case of both sides, the learned Magistrate has rejected her prayer for interim maintenance by stating therein that the petitioner is not entitled to get interim maintenance since she has a property with two storied pucca building worth of Rs. 19,00,000/-.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said property was gifted by the opposite party no. 1 in favour of the petitioner/wife
cannot be ignored.
If a person owns such a costly property, it cannot be considered that she is running with hand to mouth condition.
Rather this property evidently establishes the point that the said person has means to collect her livelihood and she has no scope to live in a state of vagrancy and destitute.

Accordingly, the learned Court below opined that at present stage as the applicant is owner of a valuable property, which may be used as good source of income to collect her livelihood, it cannot be said that she requires any kind of interim monetary help otherwise her sustenance would be at threshold.
Accordingly, the prayer for interim maintenance has been rejected.

Hence, the revisional application has come up before this Court for its disposal.
3.
On the other hand, none appears on behalf of the opposite party no. 1/husband in spite of good service.
No accommodation was sought for.
Accordingly, the case has been heard ex parte.

SUBMISSION ON BEHALF OF THE PETITIONER:

sentences.text: Learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the Petitioner submitted that the property belongs to the petitioner does not provide the monetary relief to sustain herself.
She has no income to maintain herself.
Accordingly, she is entitled to get interim maintenance from her husband, whenever he refused and neglect to maintain her.
The husband is a government's employee, his income is more than Rs. 50,000/-.
Gifting a property does not exonerate him from paying maintenance to his wife.
It is the statutory and moral obligation of the husband to maintain his wife if she has no her own income.
No sufficient materials or documents filed by the opposite party no. 1 to show that the petitioner has business of handicraft and handlooms garments as claimed.

The payslip filed by the petitioner shows his take home salary as Rs. 18,690/- even it considers as actual petitioner's income,
he is bound to maintain his wife.

4a. It is further submitted that the learned Magistrate failed to consider that the opposite party no. 1 leads illicit relationship with one Sathi Banerjee and due to their cohabitation, one child has been born and for that, a criminal case under Sections 498A/494/307 of IPC is pending against the opposite party no. 1.
Therefore, she is entitled to get interim maintenance.
Accordingly, the order passed by the learned Magistrate is liable to be set aside.

DISCUSSIONS, ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSION OF THIS COURT:
5.

Heard the submissions of the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and on perusal of the record as well as order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 2nd Court, Bolpur,
Birbhum, this Court finds it is admitted facts that both the opposite party no. 1 and petitioner are the husband and wife and their marriage was solemnized on 05.06.1990.

From the said wedlock,
one female child was born.
After three years of their marriage, she was subjected to physical and mental torture.
Furthermore, it is allegation of the petitioner that the opposite party no. 1 leads illicit relationship with one Sathi Banerjee.
Petitioner made an application under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the said application, one another application has been filed under Section 23(1) of the said Act praying for interim maintenance. 5a.
It is the settled principle of law that it is moral and legal obligation of the husband to maintain his wife if she is unable to maintain herself from her own source of income.

It is true that a two storied building was gifted by him to her during conjugal life but that does not mean that the property will provide her money to maintain herself until and unless some arrangements have been made for earning from the said property.
At the stage of considering interim maintenance allowance, the Court must have to look into the facts that whether she is able to maintain herself for her sustainability. 5b.
From perusal of the entire order, this Court does not find that she has any her own income.
It is the claim of the husband that she has a business of handicraft and handlooms garments and from there she maintains herself.
These averments are not sufficient to prove that she has income.

A cogent and documentary proof is required to be proved her income to maintain herself but no such evidence brought on record by the opposite party No.1 while considering the interim maintenance and have not produced the same.

So far as the income of the opposite party no. 1 is concerned, it is admitted facts that after deducting the EMIs for purchase of property, he is getting a total sum of Rs. 18,690/-
per month from the pay salary for December, 2016.
Even if this amount is considered as actual take home income of the opposite party no. 1, the petitioner herein is entitled to get interim maintenance to maintain herself.

Even if this Court considers the liability of the husband i.e. opposite party no. 1 and his daughter's expenses, even then Rs. 5,000/- can be allowed as an interim maintenance to the Smt Madhabilata Mondal vs Sri Haradhan Mondal And Another on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56781337/

6. Accordingly, this criminal revisional application has got merit and the impugned order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 2nd Court, Bolpur, Birbhum is liable to be set aside because the said order was passed without considering the present income of the petitioner as well as opposite party no. 1.
7.
Accordingly, CRR 1437 of 2017 is, thus, allowed ex parte.

Connected applications, if any, are also,
thus, disposed of.
8. The opposite party no
. 1 is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 5,000/- to the petitioner from the date of filing of the application under Section 23 (1) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act.

sentences.text: The interim maintenance should be paid within 10th day of each succeeding English calendar month to the petitioner and arrears of maintenance shall be paid by the opposite party no. 1 in 40 equal instalments till final realization.
9. Case Diary, if any, is to be returned to the learned Advocate for the State.

10. Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent to the learned Court below for information.
11.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
